content.comment_body: Hello, I have an AM2 analog module connected to my [product_name]. Red wire goes to L+, black wire to M, both with 24V. I'm using it to read an analog laser sensor, but now the RUN/STOP LED no longer lights up. Is there a way to reset the module, or could it be faulty?
Does the RUN/STOP LED light up in any color, such as red, orange, or yellow?
No, the LED doesn't show any light at all.

Are you certain the power supply is connected correctly? Did you measure the voltage? If the RUN/STOP LED doesn't light in any color, there may be a power issue or the module might be defective. Resetting isn't possible; you might try switching off the power supply.
I've already checked and measured 24V between L+ and M.
It appears the module might be broken. Could you provide a diagram showing how you connected your laser sensor and power supply to this module?
If the power supply is correctly connected and you measure voltage at the terminal screws but the LED doesn't light up in any color, the module is likely defective.

Alright, I'll purchase a new one. I think I understand what happened. I applied 24V to L+ and M and had the slider engaged, so it may have received 48V. The sensor was connected with the white wire to AI1.
Regardless of how the sensor is wired, the RUN/STOP LED should light up if the power supply is functioning. Based on previous feedback, it seems the sensor worked before.

Yes, that's possible. Reference the relevant PDF and ensure earth and cable shielding are correctly connected. If you applied power with the slider engaged, you could have damaged both the module and the [product_name]. Supplying + and M from one power supply to the [product_name] and expansion modules can potentially damage the whole 24VDC system.
No, that's not possible with 48VDC if the slider was engaged.
No, the [product_name] is still functioning well—I may have gotten lucky.
Hello [user_name], what did you do with the module? Earlier, you showed a video of both the sensor and module working.

Yes, that's right. Yesterday the sensor gave a constant value of -650 and it didn't change when I moved the white wire to AI2. Today, I noticed there was no light on the module. With a new module, I'll just connect L+ and M to 24V without using the slider.
It would help if you posted your wiring diagram, including the laser sensor model/type and AM2 module type. There could be a wiring mistake somewhere.

Okay. I have the laser sensor Sick powerprox WTT12L-A2563 with 4 wires—I'm using +, - and the white one (signal); the black wire is unused. + and - wires go to the same 24V as the [product_name] and the AM2. The AM2 sits next to the [product_name], the slider is engaged, and there's 24V at L+ and M at the top. The white wire is connected to AI1 at the bottom of AM2. For the new AM2, should I just wire L+ and M with 24V and avoid inserting the slider into the [product_name]?
When replacing the AM2 module, turn off the power supply for both the [product_name] and the module. Replace the AM2 and finish your wiring, then switch the power back on.
Brown = +24 VDC Blue = M (or 0 VDC) White = Analog signal output

The [product_name] displays -650 constantly because it receives no signal from the AM2. The input is zero units due to sensor settings (min = 100, max = 3100, sensor type 0, 4-20 mA), resulting in the offset of -650.

If everything is connected properly, you can slide in the AM2 module into your [product_name]. If using three wires, connect +24V and M to the sensor and route the white (analog) wire to AM2 channel I1, also connect M from the power supply to the AM2’s M1 channel. I'll provide a diagram.

Before powering up the whole system, try disconnecting the analog sensor from the AM2 module and check its values. The sensor can be set up for 4-20mA or 0-10V and different sensing ranges. Consult the manual—see page 1, chapter 5.
Did you read my previous posts? The sensor worked before with the correct settings.

Hello, I now have the new AM2. I applied 24V to L+ and M and haven't inserted the slider into the [product_name]. The white (analog) wire isn't connected yet. The module shows a red light—what does this indicate? Should I connect the white wire?
I've found the solution online. For AM2, make sure to insert the slider and supply 24V to L+ and M. Signal input should go to input 1 (bottom).
If the RUN/STOP LED shows red, it means the module isn't communicating with the adjacent module (either base or expansion module). If it shows green, communication is established.

analysis.insight_summary: Users discovered that the AM2 analog module for [product_name] stopped showing any LED light, despite correct 24V power at its terminals. They confirmed proper wiring and tried cycling power, but the module remained unresponsive. The lack of any LED indication led users to conclude the module was likely damaged, potentially due to accidental exposure to higher voltage. Attempts to reset failed, and consensus was to replace the module.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes for a reset or recovery option for non-responsive modules, or at least a clear error indication and troubleshooting guidance. Consistent and reliable LED feedback is expected when the module is powered correctly.
